title: Canonical finite coefficient deformation transport assertions
statement: Fix the finite-field datum D [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime ell, and n a natural number. BaseRing ell n is the universe lift of Z/(ell^n), with its actual finite instance. For finite commutative coefficients and compactifiable g:V→S, form sectionObject by canonical reductionSite realization of the ordinary sectionInvariant, and realizedSectionMap by reductionSiteScalarIso followed by the realized canonical sectionMap [def-pur-dnc-coefficient-section-maps]. For a quasi-compact smooth pair with closed section s, define Geometry g s to record compactifications of g and the actual Rees/normal projections and quasi-compactness of the latter. Define FibreCompatibility, LocalizationCompatibility and MixedBaseChange as the displayed commutative squares of canonical scalar and exceptional base-change maps, without a section hypothesis in MixedBaseChange. Define ChartCompatibility using the counit-normalized ordinary etale affine chart comparisons and canonical Tate scalar reassociation. Define CoordinateNormalization to require that a global normalized comparison reads as the identity on every local constant-family model after its one-fibre reading. Define NormalizedTransport as existence, uniqueness, scalar-conjugation equation, coordinate normalization, invertibility and the zero-fibre coefficient equation for the B family comparison. Finally Assertions is the conjunction of the six section-map invertibility assertions, four fibre-map invertibility assertions, unique normalized source family comparison, and these compatibility/transport properties, in exactly the original Lean order. All definitions use the actual Rees family and its actual normal cone [def-pur-noetherian-section-specialization-arrows]; no new geometric witness or coefficient orientation is chosen.
